items.title: Carter Benny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: But interestingly enough, I think in 1926 I played with Duke Ellington for two weeks . . .

ctx.x: We’ll, of course, discuss Fletcher Henderson, who you had a couple of stints with earlier, I think.

Actually, I think I had had one. I was playing with Billy Fowler’s Orchestra at a club downtown. If I remember correctly, Donald Redmond’s father died, and he had to go back to Piedmont, West Virginia, or Virginia, wherever Piedmont is, and Fletcher asked me if I could come and work in . . . substitute for Don Redmond while he was gone. So I think I asked Billy Fowler, or maybe Fletcher approached him directly, I’m not sure. But Billy said sure, it was okay. He allowed me to do it. And because it was really…

items.title: 66095_Benny Carter oral history interview
items.q: I do remember that I did sub for Harvey Boone in the Duke Ellington orchestra, and it might have been as early as 1926.

ctx.x: say important in jazz annals and important to you. What were your relations, let's say, by this time, let's say, with Duke? I mean Duke was around there -- did you know him intimately or fairly well? Did you run in to him, did you play for him now and then on occasion? Up until, say, the early thirties.

I cannot say that I knew him intimately, but at one point I do remember, and someone has told me that they spoke to Duke about this and Duke doesn't remember it, but I guess I was sort of a little insignificant as a musician around Harlem at the time -- he had a saxophone player with him named Harvey Boon, and Harvey Boon became ill and if my memory serves me properly, the Ellington band was at a club on 57th Street called Harry Richman's Club, and I sat in for Harvey Boon for a week or two -- I'm not sure what…
